processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles with solidification in Cu moulds
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Binary Fe-Al alloys prepared by vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles using Fe of 99.99% purity and Al of 99.999% purity, solidified in Cu moulds to rods usually 18 mm diameter.
For heat treatments above 300 °C specimens were enclosed in evacuated (10^-6 bar) SiO2 capsules; at 1100 °C the treatment was usually only 15 min.
Q*: water quench from 1100 °C to room temperature; quenching suppresses short-range ordering nearly completely and traps a high concentration of excess vacancies.
Subsequent 5.5% compressive straining at 10^-4 s^-1 rate at room temperature, applied before TEM observation.

structures.overall_structure: Polycrystalline, coarse-grained single-phase bcc Fe-Al solid solution of 12 at.% Al, water-quenched from 1100 °C (suppressed short-range order, quenched-in excess vacancies).

defects.type: glide bands with dislocation tangles between them

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: After 5.5% compressive straining of the quenched Fe-12%Al alloy, glide bands were observed with dislocation tangles between them (Fig. 6(a)); before deformation only few straight dislocations were present. The deformation did not initiate cell formation.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar glide concentrated in glide bands with dislocation tangles between the bands; the quenched state reduces dislocation mobility so that no cell structure forms (cell formation occurred only in the furnace-cooled alloy).
interfaces.interface_notes: The material is a single-phase bcc Fe-Al solid solution, so no phase interfaces are reported; the relevant 'interfaces' are dislocation-substructure features (glide band boundaries / tangles).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: compression test; 5.5% total compressive strain; TEM specimens taken after deformation

characterization_methods.technique: transmission electron microscopy (TEM), bright-field imaging of dislocation distributions
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Philips CM20 instrument with 200 kV; thin foils prepared by electrolytic twin jet polishing at -30 °C and 12 V using a 7:3 mixture of methanol and nitric acid (ion milling if necessary)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; specimens deformed by 5.5% compressive straining at 10^-4 s^-1 at room temperature
characterization_methods.purpose: Study the dislocation distribution after deformation of the quenched polycrystalline Fe-12%Al alloy (with 60 ppm C)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Quenched Fe-12%Al showed glide bands with dislocation tangles between them after deformation (Fig. 6(a)); before deformation only few straight dislocations were observed; the alloy showed only a weak effect of quenching (no dislocation cell formation, which occurred only in the furnace-cooled alloy). 0.4 µm scale bar in the micrographs.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: specimens etched by an alcoholic 10% nitric acid solution
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal grain boundaries and precipitates / determine grain structure
characterization_methods.key_findings: Polycrystalline Fe-Al alloys with 4-18 at.% Al showed a coarse grain structure with grain sizes of the order of 1 mm; the as-cast alloys contained no second phases.

unmapped_findings: The polycrystalline Fe-12%Al alloy (with 60 ppm C) showed only a weak effect of quenching, in contrast to the strong quench effect found for the Fe-16%Al alloy.
Real composition of the Fe-12%Al polycrystal (Table 1): 12.0 at.% (6.2 wt.-%) Al; impurity contents C 50-60 wt.ppm, Si 60-90 wt.ppm, Cu <40 wt.ppm.

In the quenched Fe-12%Al the deformation substructure consisted of glide bands with dislocation tangles between them, whereas the furnace-cooled alloy developed a dislocation cell structure; i.e. quenching before deformation also reduces dislocation mobility, which is attributed to the presence of quenched-in excess vacancies.
